page: Vultr vcg-a16-3c-32g-8vram is a Cloud GPU instance featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It provides 3 dedicated physical cores and 3 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 10.67 GB per core. The instance includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU (0.5 GPU) with 8 GB of VRAM, alongside 170 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1705.53, while the multi-core score of 5059.76 falls into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 35.06 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 26.33 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations are relatively constrained, with a Passmark database score of 2422.2 and Redis SET operations reaching 5.39 million operations per second.

The fractional NVIDIA A16 GPU with 8 GB VRAM is suited for entry-level GPU-accelerated tasks. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the server achieved 549.08 tokens per second for prompt processing and 125.03 tokens per second for text generation. However, scaling to a medium 7B model results in lower performance, yielding 11.05 tokens per second for prompt processing and 4.56 tokens per second for text generation.

This instance offers a qualitatively cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides resource density for memory-bound applications. It is best suited for lightweight machine learning inference, small-scale model testing, image processing, and development environments that benefit from hardware acceleration and local NVMe storage.
